Option B: Twentieth century topic

text: Why did Reconstruction fail?
Study the Background Information and the sources carefully, and then answer all parts
of Question 1.
Background Information
Most historians would agree that Reconstruction was, on the whole, a failure. Some argue that
the governments of Presidents Johnson and Grant lacked the political determination to make it
work. Others blame the Republicans for introducing Radical Reconstruction which, they claim,
was too extreme and alienated the South. However, there are also those who place the blame
on the South and the Democratic Party. They claim that many Southerners were determined
to deny black Americans equality and civil rights. They achieved this by the terror tactics of the
Ku Klux Klan and by introducing ‘Black Codes’ which ensured that freedmen enjoyed little in the
way of rights.
Whose fault was it that Reconstruction failed?
Source A
The new era of Reconstruction offered great promise and could have changed the history of
the USA. Freed black people put aside their enslavement and embraced education, hard work,
faith and citizenship with enthusiasm. By 1868, over 80% of black men eligible to vote had
registered, schools for black children were opening, and courageous black leaders overcame
enormous obstacles to win election to public office. For the first time, black people became
public officials and the new governments took brave action and repealed discriminatory laws.
However, it soon became clear that emancipation did not mean equality for black people and
the hope of Reconstruction quickly became a nightmare of violence and oppression. Most white
people refused to accept emancipation and black citizenship and used force to uphold white
supremacy, while the Ku Klux Klan terrorised black communities and killed countless black
people. Confederate veterans regained political control by using white supremacist language and
terror tactics of intimidation.
From an article on the internet.

Source B
The Republican-imposed governments in the Southern states proved hopelessly inefficient and
corrupt.
Content removed due to copyright restrictions.
State governments were reformed and taxation was reduced, and the new
white regimes set about legislating black people into a lowly place in the scheme of things.
From a recent history book.
Source C
Now that we know slavery is dead, we should prepare for the consequences. We have seen how
lazy and worthless the African American has become since he has been given his freedom. If
only he understood what is expected of him. But he will not understand. We need to see if there
is some lawful means by which he may become a peaceful and industrious worker. If we shut our
eyes to his faults and the inefficiency of measures being used for his guidance and control, we
are not his friend. Let us try and get him, who has little idea of what freedom is, on the right track.
The government will listen because those who have lived with the African Americans all their
lives, and know their character, are more competent to devise a system for their government than
those who do not know them and have only recently come into contact with them.
From the Milledgeville Federal Union newspaper, July 1865. The newspaper was published
in Georgia.

Source E
The Reconstruction Act is already virtually accepted by the South. It is, of course, denounced by
certain noisy ex-Rebels. If they refuse to organise their States under the Act, the Unionists (white
and black) will organise each one. The rebel States are to choose Representatives and Senators
for the Congress. It is certain that a large majority of their people will participate in the elections.
The prospect for peace and order is better than has been the case in the South for years.
Violence is less common. The good work of Reconstruction is progressing favourably and rapidly.
Those who claimed that the Radicals wanted to keep the Southern States unrepresented and in
chaos will be shown to be wrong.
From the New York Tribune newspaper, March 1867. The Tribune was owned
by Horace Greeley who was a Radical Republican at that time.
Source F
You divided the South into military districts. Your military commanders, distrusting the Southern
people and knowing that African Americans were incompetent to manage the affairs of
government, put into the government of the States a set of men from the North who were hostile
to our people in the South. They received all the revenues of the South and every dollar of taxes
went into their pockets.
When civil governments were reinstated, these men carried their power over into these
governments. A large portion of the white people of the Southern states lost the right to vote.
These governments tore the two races apart and hurled one in violent hatred upon the other,
and to this day the African American vote is massed in opposition to the whites. Not one of these
governments represents the will of the people. They are completely cut off from the traditions, the
feelings, the interests of the people of the South.
From a speech by Lucius Lamar in the House of Representatives, June 1874. Lamar had been
a Confederate soldier and was a member of the Democratic party, representing Mississippi
in Congress.

How far were the Germans justified in protesting against the Treaty of Versailles?
Study the Background Information and the sources carefully, and then answer all parts
of Question 2.
Background Information
The terms of the Treaty of Versailles were decided at the Paris Peace Conference. The peace
terms agreed by the Allies were presented to the German delegation on 7 May 1919. Both the
German delegation and people in Germany were shocked by the terms. The German Chancellor
said that the Treaty was completely unacceptable. Why should Germany lose territory? Why
should Germany disarm? Why should Germany be blamed for starting the war? Why should
Germany pay reparations? Many Germans believed that Germany had not been defeated on the
battlefield and blamed their leaders for signing the Treaty.
Did the Germans have good reason to criticise the Treaty?

Source B
After the loss of its colonies and merchant fleet, Germany will no longer be in a position to import
raw materials in sufficient quantities. An enormous part of German industry will be condemned
to extinction and it will no longer be able to provide bread and work for millions of people. The
enforcement of the Peace Treaty will lead to the deaths of several million people. This will occur
soon because the health of the population has been broken by the starvation blockade. The
Peace will impose on Germany many times the number of deaths caused by the war. Those
who sign this Treaty will be responsible for the deaths of many millions of German men, women
and children.
From the response of the German delegation to the proposed Treaty, 15 May 1919.
Source C
Germany’s responsibility is not limited to planning and starting the war. It is also responsible for
the savage way in which it was fought. At least seven million dead lie buried in Europe because
Germany wanted to satisfy its desire for domination by going to war. We will betray those who
fought to save the freedom of the world if we do not treat this war as a crime against humanity.
Justice is what the German delegation asks for. Justice is what Germany shall have. But it must
be justice for all. There must be justice for the dead and wounded. There must be justice for
the peoples who now struggle under war debts which exceed £30 billion. There must be justice
for those millions whose homes and land have been destroyed by German savagery. We have
insisted that Germany must make reparation for wrongs inflicted.
From the Allies’ letter replying to the response of the German delegation, May 1919.
Although their reply was agreed by the Allies, this letter was written by Clemenceau.

Source F
With the armistice began the humiliation of Germany. If the Republic had appealed to the
German people to stand together and resist the enemy, millions who are now hostile to the
Republic would be loyal Republicans. So long as the Treaty of Versailles remains there can be
no rebirth of the German people; no social reform of any kind! The Treaty was made to bring 20
million Germans to their deaths and to ruin the German nation. But those who made the Treaty
cannot set it aside. Our Movement has three demands:
1 Setting aside the Peace Treaty.
2 Unification of all Germans.
